chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman al-Kazzaz, from Sabbah al-Hadhdha', from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'What do you say regarding a person in Ihram who masturbates and discharges semen?' He said, 'I consider upon him the same ruling as upon the one who has intercourse with his wife while he is in Ihram: a camel (as fidya), and performing Hajj the following year.'

key_terms.بَدَنَةً: A camel (used as a specific form of sacrificial expiation)
key_terms.عَبِثَ: He masturbated or played with his private part
key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: A person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a pilgrim in Ihram who masturbates?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) establishes that voluntary sexual release while in Ihram incurs the same expiation (kaffarah) as full marital intercourse, specifically requiring the sacrifice of a camel (badanah) and performing Hajj the following year. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that the severity of the penalty is determined by the nature of the act and the state of sanctity, rather than merely the degree of physical intimacy, thereby equating masturbation with the major breach of Ihram restrictions.
